name: Neuendorf House
notes: Sheets 0 and 1 (Pawson and Silvestrin's house for the Neuendorfs on Mallorca, photographed in 2020s): a block of reddish Santanyi lime stucco (rose) with almost no windows - monolithic, flat-roofed, a low parapet round a roof terrace; a long narrow pool (30 m by about 3 m) aimed straight at a deep loggia cut into the main facade (steps up to a dark covered dining room, a horizontal slit window above); the approach is a 110 m dead-straight stepped limestone path over lawn beside a freestanding stucco wall that stays level while the land falls away, so it grows taller down the slope, ending at a narrow slit between two 9 m walls that opens into a roofless 12 m2 atrium; limestone benches against the walls; a clay tennis court; olives and holm oaks. Modelled: the 28 x 16 m two-storey block (guessed; 6,000 sq ft over two floors), the entrance tower of 9 m walls with its roofless atrium and slit, the loggia and slit window, the pool and its paving, the first 40 m of the path with a few stepped treads, the stepped wall, the tennis court (11 x 28 m, one side) and a scatter of trees. Not seen and guessed: which way the facades face and where the court stands (orientation chosen to put the pool toward the viewer), the interior (stair and rooms ignored), the full length of the path (only about 40 m shown). Placed at its town only (a private home, now a rental); nothing here places it closer than Palma.
